mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0% and rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains above 0.03 for the entire period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in non-farm payrolls signal a strong labor market that boosts corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression has a negative coefficient with p>0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high consumer spending growth, as measured by real sales of retail and food services, the S&P 500 tends to rise over the next 20 days due to improved corporate revenue outlooks.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth is above 3% year-over-year, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in the high spending regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with rising INDPRO, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.0% and non-farm payrolls growth exceeds 200,000 jobs per month, it indicates an overheating labor market that triggers inflationary pressures and subsequent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.0% and PAYEMS growth > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in the overheating labor market regime.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in housing starts and unemployment rate signals weakening housing and labor markets that reduce consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining HOUST and UNRATE fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression has a positive coefficient with p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production, the S&P 500 tends to fall over the next 5 trading days due to reduced manufacturing output and potential recessionary signals.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is declining, or Rank IC is above 0.03 in the declining production regime.
